section_entries.label: 4. Concluding remarks
section_entries.mathematical_role: Identifies Li positivity with a simple test-function subfamily of Weil positivity and relates the arithmetic constants to Stieltjes-type constants and power series.

unit_result_entry.title: Li positivity is an explicit test-function slice of Weil positivity
unit_result_entry.why_material: Multiplicative convolution turns into product under Mellin transform; self-convolution therefore gives a transform positive on the critical line. A source-stated identity shows the Li test functions fit this pattern, so their positivity has Weil's meaning while requiring only a simple explicit family.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The distinction is coverage: Weil uses a broad positivity class, whereas Li provides a concrete countable family whose sufficiency was established by the multiset theorem.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Exact conjugation convention, convolution, transform identity, and test-function equality require scan verification.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Prime-number estimates justify removal of the test-function cutoff
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The remaining zero-side limit is controlled using the prime number theorem with error term and a classical zero-free region, which make the discarded contributions decay faster than any negative power of the logarithmic cutoff.

related_synthesis_entries.limit: This does not say the Li family exhausts Weil's admissible test functions; exact identities are scan-dependent.

Convolving a function with its conjugate-reflected partner gives a transform real and positive on the critical line. Weil's criterion tests explicit-formula positivity on this broad class. An inverse Mellin identity expresses the symmetrized Li test function as such a convolution, relating Li coefficient positivity to Weil positivity.
